beats.intro: Chapter twenty-three. [[sub]]Recovery: where logs undo death itself.
beats.ground: Recall the transfer: subtract from Ravi, add to Meena, power dies between. [[q1]]The half-done half: who undoes it? [[q2]]The committed half that never reached disk: who redoes it? [[w]]Write this: every crash asks undo-what and redo-what.
beats.deferred: First scheme: delay the data. [[flow]]Write log records, keep executing, touch no database page. Commit, then redo the updates into the database. [[crash]]Power dies. Committed work may need redo. Uncommitted work needs no undo: it never reached the disk. [[w]]Write this: deferred equals delay; redo only, never undo.
beats.immediate: Second scheme: write early. [[flow]]Log old and new values, then the data page may reach disk before commit. [[fork]]Commit yes: redo if needed. Commit no: undo the early writing. [[w]]Write this: early writing forces undo plus redo; the log makes both possible.
beats.q1: Quick check. [[q]]Which recovery scheme never needs undo?
beats.shadow: Third scheme: keep the old map. [[two]]A stable shadow table, plus a changing current table. New pages go to new places. [[flip]]At commit, the root pointer flips to current. Crash before commit: the shadow mapping still rules. [[trap]]The shadow table never changes during execution; only the current one does. [[w]]Write this: flip the root, not the data.
beats.wal: One rule above all schemes. [[rule]]The log record must reach stable storage before its data page. Log before data, always. [[why]]No log first, no undo or redo later: recovery would lack the old and new values. A log record names who, what, was, will-be: T1, A, 100, 50. [[w]]Write this: log before data, with one record example.
beats.checkpoint: Logs grow forever, so plant bookmarks. [[mark]]A checkpoint forces recent history to disk and marks the spot. [[start]]Recovery starts at the bookmark, not at page one. Everything before is already safe. [[w]]Write this: checkpoint bounds where recovery starts.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Deferred delays: redo only. Immediate writes early: undo plus redo. Shadow flips the root. [[w2]]Log before data, checkpoint to bound the work. [[w3]]The single rule: committed gets redo as needed; uncommitted gets undo as needed.
beats.final2: Chapter practice. [[q]]Crash finds uncommitted changes on disk. Which scheme was running?
beats.final3: Chapter practice. [[q]]Shadow paging recovers by doing what?
beats.finish: Well done. Death undone, work redone. Next stop: B-plus trees, where sorted leaves fly.
